artboards.title: A · Atlas — result for an address
B · Survey — result for an address
What changed, and what it takes to build

annotations.text:
Two finals, built from your feedback.

Both use direction 1's page — card on the left, map full-bleed behind it — with direction 2's survey-instrument map drawing: hairline boundaries on a coordinate grid, hatching and a crosshair where your address lands.

The veil is now a partial gradient rather than a solid wash, so the map stays readable right up to the card. Headline is down from 58px to 44/46px and the field from 58px to 50/52px.

Top row is the landing page, bottom row the result page for an address.

On the result boards: every name and number is invented — 1420 Maple Street, Springfield, Greenlake County, State House 44, the candidate counts. Nothing is a real lookup, and the polygons are hand-drawn, not real district geometry.

The rail's selected row is the boundary drawn solid; the two districts that overlap it are dashed and dotted, keyed in the legend. Line style rather than colour alone, so it survives greyscale and colour-blind vision.

Details and the build notes — including where Chakra UI would and wouldn't help — are on the notes board to the right.
